correctness.rationale: At the critical attention value, for M=max(|z|,|v|)>0 the held-v flow points strictly inward at z=±M since tanh(LM)<LM. Thus for every fixed h>0 the continuous update is strictly inside the interval, and the positive convex-average jump puts the other coordinate strictly inside as well, including at gain 1. Compact-annulus continuity proves convergence for all real initial pairs, and inward invariance bounds the continuous trajectory between jumps. Nonzero nonnegative initial data give strictly positive samples after one jump: if z starts positive it cannot hit zero in finite time, and if only v starts positive, the vector field at z=0 is positive. This includes α=0; the nonlinear deficit may vanish on the first interval if v=0, without affecting the proof. For g=γ_h, q=e^(−ah), D=1−q+gq, the left stationary probability vector is (gq,1−q)/D. Its scalar component s satisfies s_next=s−(g/D)δ with δ the integrated nonlinear flow deficit, and y=z−v satisfies y_next=(1−g)(qy−δ). Positivity gives δ=O(s³) and s_next/s→1. Consequently y/s→0 by the strictly stable ratio recursion, and both states equal s+o(s), uniformly inside each dwell. Substitution into the cubic tanh deficit gives δ/s³→(dL²/3)(1−q)/a. Thus s_next^(−2)−s^(−2)→2C and telescoping gives the stated jump-time limit; t/n→h gives the real-time limit. Oddness gives the negative-quadrant limit, not a mixed-sign amplitude. Inverting C gives 1/C=(a/K)[1/g+1/(e^(ah)−1)] with K=dL²/3, yielding strict increase in g and h. For x=ah the sign of the h-derivative of C/h is the sign of gxe^(−x)−(1−e^(−x))D, strictly negative since xe^(−x)<1−e^(−x) and D≥g. This also covers g=1, and C/h→K at small h.
residual_risks: Finite trajectories corroborate the constant, not the global theorem. Strict entry is for each positive time; an initial boundary state need not have a single uniform margin as time decreases to zero. No convergence amplitude is inferred for mixed signs and no assumption extends to overshooting jumps.

value.rationale: At the critical threshold linear stability alone is inconclusive. Global attraction for the whole nonovershooting regime is useful, and the explicit sharp constant determines the real asymptotic tuning tradeoff: increasing dwell improves relaxation when measured in updates and degrades it when measured on the physical clock. The inverse-square-root exponent by itself would not resolve this question, or determine the common amplitude of both coordinates.
residual_risks: Model-specific for a regularly sampled scalar dyad; no claim of extension to larger networks, variable dwell, mixed-sign amplitudes, or overshooting updates.
